subject: GovCloud pricing waiver request for PublicWorks pilot
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@publicworks.gov>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: AWS Partner Manager <aws-pm@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GovCloud pricing waiver request for PublicWorks pilot

Hi all,

Quick summary: PublicWorks wants to run a 12-month GovCloud pilot (security scoping completed) and has asked for a Private Offer in GovCloud with a steeper-than-standard introductory discount to make procurement straightforward. They will sign a 12-month commitment and can issue a PO once we have a finalized Private Offer.

Requested ask from Deal Desk: one-time waiver of the AWS GovCloud marketplace minimum price floor so we can publish a Private Offer at 42% off list for the initial 12 months (annualized commit $180k). This discount is outside our standard marketplace pricing guardrails because GovCloud SKUs often have price floors.

Attachments: PW_PublicSector_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW), pubworks_po_template.pdf (customer procurement template).

Why this matters: PublicWorks is a reference-targeted public sector customer in a new region for Redwood; winning this pilot unlocks a broader co-sell motion with AWS and fast entry into other municipal agencies. AWS PM is on the thread to confirm process.

Next steps I need: 1) Deal Desk signoff on the one-time price-floor waiver (or an alternative route), 2) guidance on whether we publish a short-term marketplace listing or keep this strictly as a private offer, 3) any finance/legal conditions we should include on the PO/Docusign.

Thanks — I can hop on a quick call if helpful.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Exec, Public Sector
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@publicworks.gov>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GovCloud pricing waiver request for PublicWorks pilot

Connor —

Thanks for the summary. A couple quick clarifying asks before we escalate:
- Is the $180k figure ARR or committed spend across the 12 months?
- Will the customer accept a time-limited private offer (12 months) instead of a public listing?
- Any expected marketplace incentives or co-sell credit split requested by AWS?

If this is a short pilot with a confirmed PO, I think deal desk should consider a limited waiver, but we need to understand finance impact and whether AWS requires marketplace listing to enable co-sell credits. Looping in Rishi to manage the formal waiver.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Strategic Account Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: AWS Partner Manager <aws-pm@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GovCloud pricing waiver request for PublicWorks pilot

Thanks — looping in Deal Desk. A few items we need documented to evaluate:
1) Confirmed customer PO (scanned PDF or DocuSign).
2) Exact product SKU(s) and whether these are already published in GovCloud or will be new SKUs.
3) Expected co-sell credit split (Redwood vs AWS) and any AWS incentive required.
4) Business rationale for 42% discount and churn/expansion assumptions.

Two potential approaches:
A) Private Offer only (our preference for special pricing) — submit private offer to AWS Marketplace with supporting docs; we request an exception to the GovCloud floor for this one-off.
B) Temporary marketplace listing at the discounted price with an internal waiver — more complex and riskier from pricing governance.

If the customer can sign a 12-month committed PO right away, approach A is cleanest. Please also include finance contact — we will need a quick expected margin impact calc.

I'll prepare an exception request form for Marketplace Ops once we have SKUs and PO. Adding pubworks_po_template.pdf to attachments will help.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Manager, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@publicworks.gov>, AWS Partner Manager <aws-pm@amazon.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GovCloud pricing waiver request for PublicWorks pilot

Rishi/Connor —

From a contracts/partner perspective: if we proceed with a Private Offer we need to ensure the Private Offer terms include the standard Redwood limited liability and data residency clauses for GovCloud. Also confirm that AWS PM is comfortable with co-sell attribution without a public SKU — I've seen AWS accept Private Offers for co-sell if the partner manager explicitly tags the opportunity.

I recommend Connor request an AWS PM confirmation email (it can be brief) that they will enable co-sell attribution for a GovCloud private offer for this account. That will expedite Deal Desk approval.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Partner Programs
Redwood Inference
From: AWS Partner Manager <aws-pm@amazon.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@publicworks.gov>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2026 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GovCloud pricing waiver request for PublicWorks pilot

Connor/Rishi —

We can support a Private Offer in GovCloud with co-sell attribution, but Marketplace Ops will need a formal waiver request referencing the GovCloud SKU price floor. Please include: SKU(s), justification (strategic public sector reference), committed term and ARR. I have opened an internal ticket: https://aws.amazon.com/internal/ticket/MP-77288 — include this ID in your submission.

I can sign off once Marketplace Ops approves the waiver. Recommend submitting the Deal Desk form and PDF PO; AWS will expedite for public sector references.

—Amit (AWS Partner Manager)
Amit Chatterjee
AWS Partner Solutions Manager
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2026 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GovCloud pricing waiver request for PublicWorks pilot — consolidated ask and docs

Rishi — consolidated ask below for Deal Desk approval. I pulled together the materials and the customer is ready to sign DocuSign immediately if we can finalize the Private Offer price.

Deal summary:
- Customer: PublicWorks Department (municipal)
- Offer: GovCloud private offer (12 months)
- Committed annualized spend: $180,000
- Proposed price: 42% off list for initial 12-month term
- Co-sell: AWS to be credited; expected split 70/30 Redwood/AWS (to be finalized by AWS PM)
- Why: strategic reference in municipal public sector; rapid procurement via PO; pilot could lead to expanded multi-agency rollouts

Attachments: PW_PublicSector_SOW_v1.pdf, pubworks_po_template.pdf, redwood_private_offer_terms.docx
DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/ext/ABCDEF12345
AWS ticket: https://aws.amazon.com/internal/ticket/MP-77288

Requested Deal Desk decision: Approve one-time Marketplace GovCloud price-floor waiver to allow a Private Offer at 42% off list for DL-2026-0891, subject to Finance margin signoff and inclusion of standard Redwood GovCloud terms. If there is a preferred alternative (e.g., different discount cadence or rebate structure), please propose.

If approved, I'll push DocuSign to the customer immediately.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Exec, Public Sector
